text:
The stock fell slightly today as oil prices declined on easing Middle East tensions. News Thursday that U.S.-Iran peace efforts were being revived triggered a drop in crude prices, with U.S. oil falling below $104 per barrel. Refiners like Marathon Petroleum profit when the spread between crude costs and refined product prices widens; when oil prices fall sharply, that spread can compress, pressuring margins and stock prices.

The broader context is the sharp reversal from Wednesday, when oil prices spiked on Iran conflict fears and the stock jumped to $470. Yesterday's 7% drop reflected the whipsaw as geopolitical risk came off the table. With refineries running near full capacity at 92.8%, the company has limited ability to cushion margin pressure by cutting production—it's already running hard to process available barrels.
